pages.text: Each ion of nickel takes two electrons to become metal: the mass plated is m = MIt/(nF) (Faraday). Spread over the part, that is a coat of thickness m/(ρA). Push the current too hard and hydrogen bubbles and burns the coat rough.
$(thing)Set$(): Current density, Plating time.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Bath ageing: the current efficiency varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The current is over the limit: the coat burns.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): A shorter run plates more parts an hour.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Metal plated: m = MIt/(nF)$(br)Coat thickness: d = m/(ρA)
